Generated with git version 2.43.0 using SHA-1 object format.

The repository was initialized with `git init -b main`. Two deterministic,
empty commits used Signalbox Fixture <fixture@example.test> and timestamps
2000-01-01T00:00:00Z and 2000-01-02T00:00:00Z. The generator created topic,
lock-fixture, and contended at the first commit, ran `git pack-refs --all`,
then used `git update-ref` to move topic and lock-fixture to the second commit.

The successful updates left the loose reference bytes recorded here and no
`.lock` entry. A final `git update-ref` attempted to move contended while the
recorded pre-existing lock was present; Git exited 128, preserved both files,
and reported that the reference could not be locked.

The packed replacement record was produced by `git update-ref` under
`refs/replace/` followed by `git pack-refs --all`.

initial: 5b157a42f41234f041d36f0eb1f2540600127609
replacement: 3c54f8667c0ace9b4d5f3b6fbf2160859e74e138

The SHA-256 pack index was generated with the same Git version in a bare
`git init --object-format=sha256` repository. A blob containing
`real Git SHA-256 fixture\n`, its one-entry tree, and a commit authored and
committed by Signalbox Fixture <fixture@example.test> at
2000-01-01T00:00:00Z were written with `git hash-object`, `git mktree`, and
`git commit-tree`; `git update-ref refs/heads/main` and `git repack -ad`
produced the recorded version-2 index. The `.hex` file is `xxd -p` output;
the checksum and sorted object IDs are the corresponding `git verify-pack -v`
results when run with that repository as `--git-dir`.
